subject.title: feat: retain iMessage tombstones and revisions

question: Should ordinary `imsgcrawl sync` preserve absent rows through merge-by-default, or should it retain the existing replacement behavior and expose retention only through an explicit opt-in?
rationale: Both semantics are plausible, but they have materially different privacy, storage, search, and upgrade expectations for existing archives; source inspection alone cannot choose the permanent user contract.

options.title: Preserve replacement by default
options.body: Keep normal `sync` replacement-compatible and add retention only behind an explicitly named opt-in after focused compatibility tests.

options.title: Adopt merge-by-default
options.body: Approve the retention-first contract, require explicit upgrade documentation and proof for existing archives, and keep `--restore` as the clear destructive replacement path.

recommendation.title: Preserve replacement by default
recommendation.body: Keep normal `sync` replacement-compatible and add retention only behind an explicitly named opt-in after focused compatibility tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Steipete authored the proposed archive and synchronization contract and is the strongest available routing contact in the supplied history.
